newsitem.title: SYRIA: Iraqi defector says 600 arrests since Uday shot.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi defector says 600 arrests since Uday shot.

text.p: Iraq's former intelligence chief said on Saturday Iraqi authorities had arrested over 600 senior army, party and government officials following an assassination attempt on the eldest son of President Saddam Hussein.

"The arrests were made within what is called in Iraq an emergency plan which stipulates the detention of all suspected figures within the army, government and party," Wafiq al-Samerai said in an interview.
Authorities said Uday, 32, was shot by gunmen on December 12 while driving in a wealthy area of the capital. He has since been shown on television greeting well-wishers from his hospital bed.

"Those arrested included Staff Colonel Thaer Hussam al-Din, head of Uday's special bureau and several other high-ranking officers from the security forces," said Samerai, an active opposition figure based in Syria since he defected in 1994.
He said Qusay, Saddam's second son, had personally interrogated many officers including Staff Major-General Saleh Yousuf Sael, commander of the Seventh Infantry Division.

Samerai said the body of Colonel Abdullah al-Douri -- a security officer who is also coordinator of the Iraq Olympic Committee that is headed by Uday -- was found several days after the assassination attempt.

Uday blame the attack on Iran, which fought Iraq from 1980 to 1988, but there has been no official statement of who was responsible or if anyone had been arrested. Iran denied any role in the shooting.
Samerai told Reuters he thought Uday's injuries, which have not been revealed, could leave him crippled: "Sixteen days after the attack he was not shown standing."
The former intelligence chief said the Iraqi opposition was hampered by many divisions but appealed for Arabs to help those trying to topple Saddam.
"Arabs should pick up a nationalist group which is capable of replacing Saddam when the dictator is removed, today, tomorrow or a year later," he said.
